apps.name: Aave
apps.description: Aave helps users explore live Aave V3 and V4 markets, review wallet positions and DAO governance, simulate lending actions, and prepare non-custodial transactions. Every transaction is returned unsigned: the plugin reads the markets and writes the call, and the wallet stays with the user.
apps.creator: Avara

prompts.text: Where can I earn the most on stablecoins across Aave right now?
Which pays more for USDC right now, Aave V3 or V4 on Ethereum?
What's the health factor of 0x0a42b2f3a0d54157dbd7cc346335a4f1909fc02c, and how far from liquidation?

apps.name: Airtable
apps.description: Airtable lets agents list bases, read and update records, and summarize table contents. An API key from the account page is passed to the local server as one environment variable.
apps.creator: Airtable

prompts.text: What bases do I have access to?
Summarize the launch tracker table.
Mark the shipped features as done in the roadmap base.

apps.name: Apple apps
apps.tagline: Mail, Calendar and more on your Mac
apps.description: Apple apps lets agents use Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Reminders, Notes, Messages and Safari on this Mac. It works on macOS only. OpenBot starts mcp-icloud, a community server that is not made by Apple or OpenBot. The server controls the apps through AppleScript, on this computer, and needs no account and no key. When you install it, OpenBot can ask macOS for access to all of these apps at once, with one prompt for each app. If you do not, macOS asks the first time an agent uses an app. To change this later, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Automation. Agents can send email and iMessages, and change or delete events, contacts and reminders, so review each write before you approve it. What the tools read, such as email text, goes to the model provider of the agent.
apps.creator: MrGo2

prompts.text: Summarize my unread email in Apple Mail from today.
What is on my Apple Calendar today and tomorrow?
Find the latest email about the project meeting and add the meeting to my calendar.

apps.name: Atlassian
apps.tagline: Jira work items and Confluence pages
apps.description: Atlassian lets agents search and read Jira work items, Confluence pages and Bitbucket pull requests, and create or update work items, pages and comments. Each user signs in to their own Atlassian account through the browser and approves the access on a consent screen. Agents get the same permissions as the user: they can change work items and pages, change page permissions, and merge pull requests. Tools that delete Jira data stay off until an organization admin turns them on. Each tool call uses Rovo credits.
apps.creator: Atlassian

prompts.text: Which open Jira work items are assigned to me?
Find the Confluence page about our release process and summarize it.
Create a Jira work item for the login bug with steps to reproduce.

apps.name: Brave Search
apps.description: Brave Search lets agents search the web and local results without tracking. An API key from the Brave Search API dashboard is passed to the local server as one environment variable.
apps.creator: Brave

fields.label: API key
fields.hint: Brave Search API dashboard → API keys

prompts.text: What are reviewers saying about this framework version?
Find today's announcements for this product area.
Compare these two vendors with cited sources.

apps.name: Canva
apps.description: Canva lets users create and edit designs in words, search their own design library, upload and organize assets, export in the format a channel needs, and leave comments where the work is. Each user signs in to their own Canva account, and the agent can do what that account can do.
apps.creator: Canva

prompts.text: Show me my most recently edited Canva design.
Resize my launch poster for Instagram and export both as PNG.
Turn these release notes into a six-slide Canva presentation.

apps.name: ClickUp
apps.description: ClickUp lets agents search tasks, docs, comments and chat, create and update tasks, lists and docs, post comments, send chat messages and track time. Each user signs in to their own ClickUp account through the browser. Agents get the same permissions as the user. They can move tasks to the trash and delete comments.
apps.creator: ClickUp

prompts.text: Find my open ClickUp tasks due this week.
Create a ClickUp task for these action items and assign it to me.
Find the latest project update in ClickUp and summarize the open questions.

apps.name: Cloudflare
apps.description: Cloudflare lets agents list and manage Workers, DNS records, R2, D1 and KV through the Cloudflare API, query Workers logs, and search the Cloudflare docs. Each user signs in to their own Cloudflare account through the browser. On Cloudflare's consent page, choose Read only: the default, Minimal, does not let agents see Workers, logs or DNS records. With write permissions, agents can deploy and delete Workers, change DNS records and change other account settings.
apps.creator: Cloudflare

prompts.text: Which Workers are deployed in my Cloudflare account?
Which Cloudflare Workers logged errors in the last hour?
List the DNS records of each zone in my Cloudflare account.

apps.name: Cobrain
apps.tagline: Shared memory for your AI agents
apps.description: Cobrain is a Markdown memory that every AI you connect can read and write. Agents load the context of a client or project before working, search past notes and decisions, and save what they learn so the next thread starts where the last one ended. Each user signs in to their own Cobrain account.
apps.creator: Cobrain

prompts.text: Load my Cobrain context for this project before we start.
Search my Cobrain notes for what we decided about pricing.
Save a note in Cobrain with what we did today and what is left.

apps.name: Coinbase
apps.description: Coinbase lets agents read prices, balances, portfolios, orders and fees in Coinbase Advanced Trade, preview and place orders, convert between assets, and move funds between portfolios. Each user signs in to their own Coinbase account through the browser. Agents get the same permissions as the user. Orders and conversions use real funds, and agents can pay for x402 requests from the USDC balance.
apps.creator: Coinbase

prompts.text: What are my Coinbase balances in each portfolio?
Show the BTC-USD price on Coinbase and how it moved this week.
Preview a 50 USD market buy of ETH on Coinbase. Do not place the order.

apps.name: Composio
apps.tagline: Many apps through your own Composio link
apps.description: Composio connects agents to Gmail, Slack, GitHub, and hundreds of other apps through one MCP server. Connect the apps you want in your Composio account, then paste its MCP URL and API key here.
apps.creator: Composio

fields.label: MCP URL
fields.hint: The URL of an MCP server in your Composio account

fields.label: API key
fields.hint: Find it in your Composio account, in Settings > Sessions & API Key.

prompts.text: Summarize my unread email and draft replies to the urgent ones.
Post a summary of this pull request to our team channel.
Which apps and actions can you use through Composio?

apps.name: Context7
apps.description: Context7 fetches current documentation and API references for libraries and frameworks, so answers use the version the project actually runs. It needs no account and no key.
apps.creator: Upstash

prompts.text: What is the current API for virtualized lists in this framework?
What changed between v2 and v3 of this router?
Show a current example for authenticated file uploads.

apps.name: Figma
apps.description: Figma lets agents read design files, inspect components, styles and variables, and hand production specs to engineers. It connects to the MCP server in the Figma desktop app, on this computer. The server can read designs only; write support is in progress.
apps.creator: Figma
steps: Open the Figma desktop app and sign in. The server needs a Dev or Full seat on a paid plan.
Open a design file from a team project, not from Drafts.
Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows), search for "MCP", and turn on "Enable desktop MCP server".
Keep Figma open while agents use it.

prompts.text: Hand off the checkout file: list screens, components, and styles.
Audit this file for inconsistent spacing and color use.
Extract the marketing icons at 2x for the app bundle.

apps.name: Firecrawl
apps.description: Firecrawl lets agents scrape pages, extract structured data, and search the web through one API. An API key from the Firecrawl dashboard is passed to the local server as one environment variable.
apps.creator: Firecrawl

prompts.text: Extract the pricing table from this page as structured data.
Research competitor pricing and cite each source page.
What changed on our changelog page this month?

apps.name: Higgsfield
apps.description: Higgsfield lets agents generate images, videos, characters and audio with Higgsfield models such as Seedance, Kling, Veo and MiniMax Hailuo, check the credit balance, and browse the Asset Library. Results are saved to the user's Higgsfield Assets. Each user signs in to their own Higgsfield account through the browser. Every generation uses credits of that account at standard rates, also on an unlimited plan.
apps.creator: Higgsfield

prompts.text: How many Higgsfield credits do I have?
Make a Higgsfield product photo of a ceramic mug on a wooden table.
Make a 5-second Higgsfield video of waves at sunset.

apps.name: Hugging Face
apps.tagline: Models, datasets and papers on the Hub
apps.description: Hugging Face lets agents search models, datasets, Spaces, collections and papers on the Hugging Face Hub, read model cards and repository files, preview datasets, and search the Hugging Face documentation. It uses public Hub data and needs no account and no key. The tools only read: agents cannot create repositories or run jobs.
apps.creator: Hugging Face

prompts.text: Find small open models for speech recognition on Hugging Face.
Which papers are trending on Hugging Face today?
Find a dataset of weather time series and show its columns.

apps.name: Linear
apps.description: Linear lets agents list assigned issues, triage the backlog, update statuses, and draft new issues in the workspace the signed-in account belongs to. Each user signs in to their own Linear account through the browser.
apps.creator: Linear

prompts.text: What is assigned to me this week?
Triage the backlog: what is stale, blocked, or missing an owner?
File an issue for the crash in the sync queue with reproduction steps.

apps.name: Neon
apps.description: Neon lets agents list projects and branches, run SQL, read table schemas, test schema changes on a temporary branch, find slow queries, and search the Neon docs. Each user signs in to their own Neon account through the browser and can choose read-only access when they authorize. With full access, agents can run SQL that changes or deletes data, and create, reset or delete branches, databases and projects. Neon recommends its MCP server for development and testing, not for production databases.
apps.creator: Neon

prompts.text: Which projects and branches are in my Neon account?
Which queries are the slowest on my Neon database, and why?
Add an index on the orders table in a temporary branch, and show me the result before you apply it.

apps.name: Netlify
apps.description: Netlify lets agents list projects and deploys, read edge request logs, create projects, and deploy code to an existing project. Each user signs in to their own Netlify account through the browser. Agents get the same access as the user's account: they can change environment variables, forms and visitor access, install or remove extensions, and delete form submissions and environment variables.
apps.creator: Netlify

prompts.text: What is the status of the latest deploy of each of my Netlify projects?
Which URLs of my site returned server errors in the last day?
Deploy this folder to my existing Netlify project.

apps.name: Notion
apps.description: Notion lets agents read and write pages, search the workspace, and keep meeting notes and specs where the team already works. Each user signs in to their own Notion account through the browser.
apps.creator: Notion

prompts.text: Find the current launch spec and summarize the open questions.
Turn these bullets into a structured meeting note in my team space.
Update the onboarding doc with the new release checklist.

apps.name: Obsidian
apps.description: Obsidian lets agents search, read and write the notes in your vault, so the vault can be their memory. The local server connects to the Local REST API plugin in the Obsidian app on this computer. The plugin's API key is passed to the local server as one environment variable. Keep Obsidian open while agents use it.
apps.creator: Obsidian

fields.label: API key
fields.hint: In Obsidian, open Settings > Local REST API. Copy the API key and turn on "Enable non-encrypted (HTTP) server".

prompts.text: What do my notes say about the decisions on this project?
Save this decision as a new note in my vault.
Add a summary of today's work to my Work log note.

apps.name: Paper
apps.tagline: Design canvas built on HTML and CSS
apps.description: Paper lets agents read and write the design file that is open in Paper Desktop: inspect artboards, selections, computed styles, JSX and tokens, and create or change frames, text and styles. Install Paper Desktop, open it once, and open a file before you start. OpenBot starts the Paper CLI that Paper Desktop installs. Paper needs no key. Write tools change the open file, so review each write before you approve it.
apps.creator: Paper

prompts.text: Implement the selected Paper frame in this codebase, with our code conventions.
Use the styles in this repository and design a settings page in Paper.
List the design tokens in the open Paper file and compare them with our theme.

apps.name: PostHog
apps.description: PostHog lets agents query events and funnels, inspect feature flags, and summarize what changed after a release. A personal API key from the project settings goes into one Authorization header.
apps.creator: PostHog

fields.label: Personal API key
fields.hint: PostHog Project settings → Personal API keys

prompts.text: How does the signup funnel look for the last 14 days?
Which feature flags are enabled for this user?
Did activation change after last week's release?

apps.name: Prisma
apps.tagline: Postgres databases, backups and Compute apps
apps.description: Prisma lets agents list and create Prisma Postgres databases, read schemas, run SQL, list backups and restore them to a new database, manage Object Storage buckets, read Compute builds and logs, and search the Prisma docs. Each user signs in to their own Prisma account through the browser and selects a workspace. Agents get full access: they can run SQL that changes or deletes data, update schemas, delete databases and buckets, and stop, roll back or delete Compute deployments.
apps.creator: Prisma

prompts.text: Which databases are in my Prisma workspace?
Show me all available backups of my database.
Show the runtime logs of my latest Compute deployment.

apps.name: Railway
apps.description: Railway lets agents list projects and services, create projects, redeploy services, and manage feature flags. Agents can also give multi-step work to the Railway Agent, which reads logs, finds why a deploy failed, creates services and sets variables. Each user signs in to their own Railway account through the browser and chooses the workspaces and projects that agents can use. Agents get full access in those projects: they can deploy staged changes, delete feature flags, and change services, variables, databases and networking through the Railway Agent.
apps.creator: Railway

prompts.text: Which projects and services are in my Railway workspace?
Why does my backend service on Railway crash on deploy?
Redeploy the API service in my Railway project.

apps.name: Render
apps.description: Render lets agents list workspaces and services, read logs, events and metrics, see the deploy history, trigger deploys, and run read-only SQL on Render Postgres. A Render API key goes into one Authorization header. The key reaches every workspace of the Render account. Agents can create web services, static sites, cron jobs, Postgres databases and Key Value instances, which can cost money, and they can replace the environment variables of a service. The server cannot delete a resource.
apps.creator: Render

prompts.text: Which services are in my Render workspace?
Which errors did my Render web service log in the last hour?
Why did the last deploy of my Render service fail?

apps.name: Resend
apps.description: Resend lets agents send transactional email and check delivery through one API. An API key from the Resend dashboard is passed to the local server as one environment variable.
apps.creator: Resend

prompts.text: Send the launch announcement draft to the beta list.
Did the invoice email reach the customer?
Draft a password-reset email for the new flow.

apps.name: RevenueCat
apps.description: RevenueCat lets agents read and change the setup of your in-app subscriptions: apps, products, entitlements, offerings, packages, paywalls and experiments. Agents can also look up customers and their purchases, and read charts and metrics. A RevenueCat secret API key goes into one Authorization header. The key reaches one project. With a read-only key, agents can only read. With a write key, agents can submit products to the App Store for review, grant entitlements to customers, and delete packages, targeting rules and webhooks.
apps.creator: RevenueCat

fields.label: API key
fields.hint: In the RevenueCat dashboard, open API keys in your project and create a secret API key. A read-only key is enough to view data.

prompts.text: Which offerings and packages does my RevenueCat project have?
How did my RevenueCat revenue and active subscriptions change this month?
Which entitlements does this RevenueCat customer have, and when do they expire?

apps.name: Robinhood
apps.description: Robinhood lets agents read the accounts, positions, balances, transaction history and watchlists of a Robinhood customer, read market data, and place stock, options and crypto orders. Each user signs in to their own Robinhood account through the browser. At the first sign-in, Robinhood asks the user to open a separate Agentic account. Agents can trade only in that account, and by default they place orders without asking the user to approve each one.
apps.creator: Robinhood

prompts.text: Summarize my Robinhood positions and how they moved today.
How did each stock on my Robinhood watchlist move this week?
How much cash is in my Robinhood Agentic account?

apps.name: Sentry
apps.description: Sentry lets agents search recent errors, inspect stack traces and affected releases, and summarize what broke after a deploy. Each user signs in to their own Sentry account through the browser.
apps.creator: Sentry

prompts.text: What new errors appeared since yesterday's deploy?
Explain the top crash in the mobile project and its likely cause.
How healthy is the current release compared to the last one?

apps.name: Stripe
apps.description: Stripe lets agents look up payments, customers, and invoices, and draft payment links, in the account the signed-in user can reach. Each user signs in to their own Stripe account through the browser.
apps.creator: Stripe

prompts.text: Look up this payment and explain why it failed.
Summarize this customer's invoices and outstanding balance.
Draft a payment link for the Pro plan at 49 per month.

apps.name: Supabase
apps.description: Supabase lets agents list projects, run SQL, read table schemas and logs, check security and performance advisors, manage edge functions and branches, and search the Supabase docs. Each user signs in to their own Supabase account through the browser and chooses an organization. Agents get full access: they can run SQL that changes or deletes data, apply migrations, deploy edge functions, and create or pause projects.
apps.creator: Supabase

prompts.text: Which projects are in my Supabase organization?
List the tables and columns of my Supabase database.
Which errors did my Supabase project log in the last hour?

apps.name: TickTick
apps.description: TickTick lets agents search and filter tasks, add and update tasks, and manage lists, sections, folders, tags and comments. Agents can also read and change habits and focus records, and read events from the calendars connected to TickTick. Each user signs in to their own TickTick account through the browser. Agents get read and write access: they can complete, move and delete tasks, and delete tags and focus records.
apps.creator: TickTick

prompts.text: Which TickTick tasks are due today?
Add these action items to my TickTick Inbox.
Which TickTick tasks did I complete last week?

apps.name: Todoist
apps.description: Todoist lets agents find tasks by date, text, label or filter, add and reschedule tasks, and manage projects, sections, labels, comments and reminders. Each user signs in to their own Todoist account through the browser. Agents get read and write access: they can change, complete and delete tasks, projects and other items.
apps.creator: Doist

prompts.text: Which Todoist tasks are due today?
Add these action items to my Todoist Inbox.
Move my overdue Todoist tasks to tomorrow.

apps.name: Trello
apps.description: Trello lets agents search and read boards, lists, cards, checklists and comments, create boards and cards, move lists and cards, mark cards done, and add checklists, comments and labels. Agents can also read and add cards in the user's Trello Inbox, and read Planner events, which can come from a connected Google or Outlook calendar. Each user signs in to their own Trello account through the browser and chooses the workspaces on a consent screen. Agents get the same permissions as the user in those workspaces. They can archive cards and lists, but the server cannot delete anything permanently.
apps.creator: Atlassian

prompts.text: Which Trello cards are assigned to me?
Summarize what is in progress on my Trello board.
Add these action items as cards to my Trello board.

apps.name: Vercel
apps.description: Vercel lets agents list projects and recent deployments, read build and runtime logs, and find why a build failed. Each user signs in to their own Vercel account through the browser and chooses the teams that agents can use. In those teams, agents get the same rights as the user's account. They can also change environment variables, domains, DNS records and deployments, and buy domains.
apps.creator: Vercel

prompts.text: Why did the last production deployment fail?
List the deployments from today and their status.
Which routes had runtime errors in the last hour?
